prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation supplies transformer/feeder bays. Bay Automation Controller(Juniper) validates authority/mode/availability; executes approved-logic/interlock-permitted commands, compares indications, flags discrepancies, associates Breaker Inspection Tag, uses Battery Load Test Record, sends Bay Status Digest→Station Supervisory Control System(Glasswing). Glasswing displays authorized controls/quality/staleness/results, retains alarms/events, produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip, receives Protocol Retry Summary←Station Gateway(boundary-preserving mapped traffic/timestamps/quality/errors; no equipment-state changes). Breaker Control Unit returns position/circuit-health, rejects nonpermissive commands; control failures cannot inhibit protection. North Bay Controller blocks unready closes/preserves local control during supervisory loss; South Bay Controller reports mode/availability; non-substitutable scopes. Feeder Protection Relay(Tandem) trips independently using approved settings, produces Relay Diagnostic Note; communications/testing cannot compromise protection. North Protection Panel preserves independent zone/trip paths; Transformer Protection Panel independently protects transformers. Satellite Time Receiver(Bluefin) sends quality-checked time/Clock Drift Snapshot→Sequence Event Archive(Orchard): authoritative time-ordered events/outcomes/testing/restoration, source/order/quality/uncertainty; investigate timing concerns before sequence analysis. Engineering Workstation: authorized change-controlled configuration/review/export; Settings Review Receipt→Maintenance Remote Terminal(maintenance-only/no-bypass). Station DC System monitors supplies/loss, retains Battery Load Test Record; verify availability before control-power-dependent switching. Control Room Operator decides automation appropriateness, requests switching, acknowledges alarms, records restrictions, locally verifies uncertain remote status, tracks disabled protection through restoration; Clearance Handoff Memo→Switching Desk Coordinator(Keystone), reconciled with switching record. Keystone checks authority/state/communication limits/prerequisites/conflicts/clearances, maintains ordered switching/holds/stops, produces Isolation Boundary Card, confirms handback. Substation Supervisor authorizes/escalates/controls changes, coordinates Keystone; verifies records, cleared restrictions, risk owners/dispositions before normal service. Protection Relay Engineer(Larkspur) reviews settings/coordination/material-change behavior/tests/restoration; records concerns; assesses unexplained trips/abnormal indications before reinstatement. Substation Field Crew(Cinder) verifies identity/status/clearance/isolation/grounding/card-defined boundaries; produces condition/time Breaker Inspection Tag; promptly reports abnormalities, pauses uncertain-boundary work. Require loading/switching/staffing planning, approved tests/calibrated

New part:
S240: The Maintenance Remote Terminal shall use controlled access, and each maintenance session shall be attributable to an authorized user.
S241: The North Bay Controller shall be checked for expected local behavior after approved configuration work.
S242: The South Bay Controller shall be checked for expected local behavior after approved configuration work.
S243: The North Protection Panel shall remain available for independent protection functions during supervisory control interruptions.
S244: The Transformer Protection Panel shall remain within its approved settings and operating constraints during handover.
S245: Periodic operational reviews shall examine command outcomes, event records, exceptions, and corrective actions so that automation decisions remain traceable and safe.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
